clue.text: Over that one cannot take stock

definitions.text: Over that one cannot take stock

blocks.clueFragment: Over that one cannot take stock
blocks.note: surface reading: something that stops you assessing your goods or inventory
setter's reading: stock means farm animals, which cannot be driven across this barrier of bars in a road

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper finds some obstacle preventing the annual stocktake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take stock' is the idiom for reviewing your position; here stock is livestock that will not walk over the bars.
explanation.definitionFit: A grid of spaced bars across a road lets vehicles pass while hooves slip, so livestock will not cross it.

clue.text: Side with rogue having toppled leader

indicators.note: toppling the leader removes the head, so the word drops its first letter

blocks.note: a scamp is a rascal

explanation.surface: A faction joins a rebel after the leader is overthrown.
explanation.definitionFit: A faction or group sharing a view in a dispute, such as the rival camp, is one side.

clue.text: People in wrongful act, suffering

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the following phrase's word

blocks.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
men are people

explanation.surface: People committing a wrongful act are in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: A tort is a legal term for a civil wrong that gives grounds for damages.
explanation.definitionFit: Anguish or severe pain, physical or mental, is a noun synonym for suffering.

clue.text: Expert aligned cryptically with clue

indicators.note: cryptically means in a disguised way, so the letters are rearranged to hide them

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
a light is something that sheds understanding, as a hint does

explanation.surface: A crossword expert lines things up cleverly with a clue.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords a light is also the word an answer fills in the grid, which fits the crossword surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A prominent and influential figure in a field is an authority, so the phrase can mean an expert.

clue.text: Hold on, calm down!

blocks.note: first meaning: literally take a firm hold
second meaning: an order to regain self-control

explanation.surface: Someone tells a panicking person to wait and settle.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means literally to clutch something firmly and, as an idiom, to regain control of your emotions.

clue.text: Gangway for the audience? Absolutely!

blocks.note: a gangway between rows of seats is an aisle, and the contraction for I will sounds the same
what you say is delivered for listeners, and the phrase also tells you the gangway word is heard rather than read

explanation.surface: An usher asks whether there is a passage for spectators, and is told of course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For the audience' does double duty: it marks the gangway word as heard, and it supplies the word for speaking to listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is an emphatic way of agreeing, much like saying definitely or certainly.

clue.text: Source of oil in hand

definitions.note: the palm is the inner part of the hand rather than the whole hand

blocks.note: first meaning: the tropical tree whose fruit is pressed for oil
second meaning: the flat inner surface of the hand

explanation.surface: Someone holds a little bottle of oil in their hand.
explanation.definitionFit: The oil palm is a tree grown for its fruit oil, and the palm is also the inside face of a hand.

clue.text: Further remark about two riders initially on horseback?

indicators.note: initially points to the first letters of the two words before it
about means around, so the remark wraps round the two letters

blocks.note: an aside is an extra comment made in passing
the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Someone comments on two jockeys sitting on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that horseback is one example of the position: you can sit this way on a chair or wall too.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting with one leg each side of something is how a rider sits a horse.

clue.text: What I delight in not at all

blocks.note: first meaning: the thing that gives me joy
second meaning: a polite reply to thanks

explanation.walkthrough: 'Not at all' looks like a flat denial, but here it is the courteous answer to someone's thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally it is the joy belonging to me, and as a set phrase it politely acknowledges gratitude.

clue.text: Yours truly has played clarinet in commercial

indicators.note: an instrument that is played is worked over, so the word clarinet is jumbled here

blocks.note: the setter refers to themselves as yours truly
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of playing the clarinet in a TV advertisement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commercial' looks like a noun meaning an advert, but it is the adjective being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercantile describes trade and merchants, so it is a synonym of commercial as an adjective about business.

clue.text: First of all, some turbulence experienced, petrifying part of flight

indicators.note: first of all asks for the first letter of every one of the following words

blocks.note: the opening letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A nervous passenger describes being terrified by turbulence on a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests aeroplanes, but a flight here is a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of stairs is made up of individual treads, each one a single stair you climb.

clue.text: Pole no better, used for levering device

indicators.note: used means worked over or exploited, so the letters are reworked into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A pole is no better than anything else for prising something up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a lever, which fits the surface, but it is just letters for rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: This kitchen tool prises off crown caps by levering against the rim of a bottle.

clue.text: Located in arcade, liquor shop

indicators.note: located in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the end of arcade joined to the start of liquor

explanation.surface: A liquor store is found in a shopping arcade.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicatessen is a small food store, commonly shortened, selling cooked meats and cheeses.

clue.text: A girl some drunk put on a pedestal

indicators.note: a drunk person is all over the place, so the letters before it lose their order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tipsy girl is idolised by someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To idealise or romanticise something is to make it seem more attractive than it is, as if on a plinth.

clue.text: Where satellite dish might be free

blocks.note: first meaning: literally mounted on a building's roof or wall
second meaning: paid for by the establishment

explanation.surface: A satellite dish is offered without charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish' suggests food served free, which is the idiom's real home in pubs and restaurants.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish fixed to a home sits on it, and drinks provided at the landlord's expense are given gratis.

clue.text: Cry of exasperation, a nation having failed to invest capital in growth

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its first letter, here of the next word
something that has failed has broken down, so the letters of a nation are broken up
to invest is to clothe or surround, so the jumbled letters wrap round the single letter

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
its first letter

explanation.surface: An economist sighs that a country has failed to put money into growth.
explanation.definitionFit: Exasperated people say this phrase when an annoying thing happens yet another time.

clue.text: Highlight emotional tension

blocks.note: first meaning: to emphasise
second meaning: mental strain

explanation.surface: A therapist points out the anxiety in a client.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to emphasise a point; as a noun it is mental strain and worry.

clue.text: Reserve staff gathering in library?

blocks.note: to book is to reserve
a club is a heavy stick or staff

explanation.surface: Library staff reserve a room for a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like employees, but it is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of readers meeting regularly to discuss novels might well meet among library shelves.

clue.text: That man has check enclosed

blocks.note: the pronoun for that man
to rein in is to check or restrain

explanation.surface: A man has a cheque included in an envelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' looks like the American spelling of a bank cheque, but it means restrain.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal letters say a document is found herein, meaning contained in this one, so it works as enclosed.

clue.text: Type of wine in claret’s in abundance

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

blocks.note: spans the end of claret's, all of in, and the start of abundance

explanation.surface: There is plenty of a kind of wine within a supply of claret.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white flavoured with pine resin, so it is one variety among wines.

clue.text: European celebrity, 3 down?

blocks.note: a native of Poland
a famous person

explanation.surface: A famous Polish person is described as a guiding figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to the answer at 3 down, LEADING LIGHT; the question mark shows the northern star is a figurative example of one.
explanation.definitionFit: The north star guides navigators, so it is literally a light that leads travellers, matching that other entry.

clue.text: Athlete with javelin, say, is avoiding this athlete with blade

indicators.note: avoiding means keeping away from, so the word before it is taken out of the word after

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, the letters to be removed
an oar's flat end is its blade

explanation.surface: A javelin competitor keeps away from a rower.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'is' is removed from 'this', leaving two letters to put before the oarsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A javelin competitor hurls the spear in field events; the 'say' marks it as one example among discus and hammer.

clue.text: Cake scoffed in old European region, unfinished

indicators.note: unfinished means the region's name lacks its last letter
in places the first word inside the shortened region

blocks.note: the ancient Roman name for the land roughly covering France
to scoff is to eat greedily

explanation.surface: A cake is devoured somewhere in ancient Europe before the meal is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffed' could mean mocked, but here it is the British sense of wolfed down.
explanation.definitionFit: Gâteau is the French word for a rich layered dessert, commonly used in English for such a sponge.

clue.text: Start second car

blocks.note: to hatch a plan is to set it going
to second a motion is to back it

explanation.surface: A driver starts the second car.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a style of motor vehicle with a rear door that swings upward to the boot.

clue.text: Briefly, do bit

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: Someone is told to do their share, quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like a verb, but it is the noun for a social gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece or portion of something whole is a synonym for a bit.

clue.text: Drop round line for rod

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the first word goes about the next

blocks.note: to axe something is to drop or cancel it
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Someone is told to put down a fishing line and take a rod instead.
explanation.definitionFit: The shaft on which wheels turn is a metal bar, so it can be called a rod.

clue.text: Single item, that object behind Parisian article

indicators.note: behind says the pronoun phrase comes after the French word, not before it as printed

blocks.note: the French indefinite article
the pronoun for a thing

explanation.surface: A shopper picks out one thing displayed behind a French newspaper article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' places the pronoun after the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: A single component or one thing counted as a whole is called by this word.

clue.text: Something melted when angel I saw transported by kiss

indicators.note: transported means carried elsewhere, so the letters before it are moved around

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
X is the kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Someone melted on seeing an angel and was carried away by a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' means next to, so the kiss sits beside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This wax is heated until runny and dripped onto envelopes and documents, then stamped to fasten them.

clue.text: Cheese, shaped wheels

indicators.note: a word that wheels turns round, so shaped is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: something shaped has been made

explanation.surface: Cheese is shaped into wheels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wheels' looks like a noun for rounds of cheese, but it is a verb meaning turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: This mild Dutch variety comes in round balls coated with red wax.

clue.text: Third masseur less hot for life in the tropics

indicators.note: less means minus, so the following abbreviation is taken away

blocks.note: a masseur rubs people's muscles
read loosely as the number three
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A third massage therapist is less heated about life in a hot country.
explanation.walkthrough: The number word loses its H and goes after the masseur's word.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant tapped for latex is a living thing growing in tropical regions, so it is life found there.
